featured.headline: COP31 hits its final day with no deal in sight

featured.summary: The UK PM meets EU leaders to sign a reset on food checks, energy and youth mobility: 100,000 visas a year for under-32s.

featured.headline: A quarter of the world's children live in war zones
featured.summary: Save the Children says nearly one in four children now lives in a conflict zone, the highest share it has ever recorded.

featured.headline: Antibiotics are failing and patients are out of options
featured.summary: A UN report warns common infections are becoming untreatable as drug resistance spreads, leaving doctors few working antibiotics.

featured.headline: AI is remaking government, but the divide persists
featured.summary: A new UN survey finds AI is transforming public administration worldwide, while poorer countries fall further behind on digital services.

featured.headline: No state permission needed to associate, UN rules
featured.summary: The UN Human Rights Committee says freedom of association does not require state authorisation, in a new interpretation.

featured.headline: 65,000 tents wait to enter Gaza as winter nears
featured.summary: Nearly 65,000 approved tents are still waiting to enter Gaza while families face winter in damaged shelters, officials say.

featured.headline: UN could soon be leaderless as Guterres race stalls
featured.summary: The race to succeed Antonio Guterres has stalled, leaving the UN facing a possible leadership vacuum, diplomats say.
